Data types and arguments of code generation routines

Source: R/codegen-utilities.R
codegen-datatypes.Rd

DataType() holds the names of a data type in the target languages, and get_default_datatype() chooses one for an expression, as in sympy.utilities.codegen. InputArgument(), OutputArgument(), InOutArgument() and Result() describe the arguments and results of a routine made by make_routine(); their fields are read with ast_attr().

Usage

DataType(cname, fname, pyname, jlname, octname, rsname)

get_default_datatype(expr, complex_allowed = NULL)

InputArgument(name, datatype = NULL, dimensions = NULL, precision = NULL)

OutputArgument(
  name,
  result_var,
  expr,
  datatype = NULL,
  dimensions = NULL,
  precision = NULL
)

InOutArgument(
  name,
  result_var,
  expr,
  datatype = NULL,
  dimensions = NULL,
  precision = NULL
)

Result(
  expr,
  name = NULL,
  result_var = NULL,
  datatype = NULL,
  dimensions = NULL,
  precision = NULL
)

Arguments

cname, fname, pyname, jlname, octname, rsname

The type names in C, Fortran, Python, Julia, Octave and Rust.

expr

An expression.

complex_allowed

Whether a complex type is allowed. NULL reads the option symcompR.complex_allowed (default FALSE), which plays the part of SymPy's module flag COMPLEX_ALLOWED.

name

A symbol (or, for Result(), a name).

datatype

A DataType().

dimensions

A list of list(lower, upper) bounds.

precision

The precision, or NULL.

result_var

The variable or element the result is stored in.

Value

An object of the corresponding class.

Examples

x <- Symbol("x")
get_default_datatype(x)
#> <DataType double> 
InputArgument(x)
#> InputArgument(x)
